increments.title: The collector accepts, keeps, persists, serves and announces a run's state
increments.goal: Give the collector an endpoint of its own that accepts a run's backlog state, keep the latest state per run, serve the runs it holds and the full state of one over its JSON API behind the existing authentication, persist it across a restart, and announce every write on the existing SSE stream.
criteria: A POST of a run's state to an endpoint of the collector's own is accepted and identified by the issue the state belongs to; a second POST for the same run replaces what was held for it, so the collector keeps the latest state per run and no history.

The JSON API answers both questions: the runs the collector holds, with what a reader needs to pick one including when each was last written, and the full state of one named run; asking for a run it does not hold answers 404.
The new ingest endpoint and the new read endpoints sit behind the collector's existing authentication and reject an unauthenticated caller exactly as its other endpoints do.
A collector restarted against the same measurement directory still serves the run state it held, persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted.
A write to a run's state puts a frame on the existing /api/stream SSE stream that tells an already-connected client which run changed.

tools/argus/README.md documents what the collector now accepts and serves, and tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Accepted at review round 0 with no findings: npm --prefix tools/argus test (179 cases, exit 0) and ./test.sh (6 suites, exit 0). It fixed the wire contract the two open increments build against: POST /api/runs with the run id and the whole backlog document, GET /api/runs listing id, issue, workflow, increment count and updatedAtMs latest-write-first, GET /api/runs/:id serving one state whole with 404 for a run not held, all behind the existing token gate, persisted as runs.jsonl and announced as an uncoalesced SSE frame naming the run and its update time. Merged into claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr.

increments.title: The recorder pushes the state it just wrote, best-effort and invisible
increments.goal: Make the recorder send the run's state to the configured collector after every write it makes, without changing anything an agent or a workflow sees and without ever costing a run a failure, a wait or a line of output.
criteria: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote to the collector's run-state endpoint, identified by the issue the state belongs to, so a collector that receives it then serves that exact document under that issue.
The recorder stays the only writer of backlog.json and keeps its zero dependencies; no agent page and no workflow prompt changes, so how an agent calls the recorder is exactly what it is today.
The collector's address and its credential are read from the same OTLP collector environment the rest of uroboros already exports for argus, and from nowhere else.
With no collector configured in the environment, the recorder does nothing extra.

A collector that is unreachable, slow or refusing costs the recorder neither a non-zero exit nor a wait beyond a short timeout, and produces no output: the exit codes and the one confirmation line of every subcommand stay byte-identical to today's.
skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md is current for the cases and helpers this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Accepted at review round 0 with no findings: node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs (30 cases, exit 0) and ./test.sh (6 suites, exit 0). One send site after the dispatch switch POSTs { id, state } to <base>/api/runs after init, record, branch and close, read sending nothing; the address and credential come from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS with UROBOROS_OBS_URL/UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN as the second name pair, and from nowhere else; the send is bounded by a 2s AbortSignal timeout inside an empty catch, so an unreachable, stalling or refusing collector costs no exit code, no wait and no output. Verified on Node 20, 21 and 22. No agent page, workflow prompt or argus file changed. Merged into claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr.

increments.title: argus-ui gains a run view: one run's backlog, switchable and live
increments.goal: Give the interface a run view beside its session view that shows a run's backlog as the collector serves it, opens on the most recently written run, lets the reader switch runs, and updates itself over the collector's SSE stream.
criteria: The interface shows a run view beside its existing session view, holding for the run it shows: the issue and the workflow it belongs to and when it was last written; the increments in the backlog's order, each with its id, title, status, branch and note; a count of how many increments are closed and how many are open; and the codemap.
A closed increment reads as closed, with its status and its note.

The view opens on the run written to most recently and the reader can switch to any other run the collector holds, taking both the list of runs and the one run's whole state from the collector's run endpoints and from no other source.

A write to the shown run's state reaches an already-open page live over the collector's Server-Sent-Events stream, whose frame names only which run changed and when: no polling, no reload, no manual refresh.
The existing session view, its timeline and its stream handling keep working unchanged beside the new view.
argus-ui still imports nothing outside itself and reads no uroboros file; test/independence.test.mjs still guards exactly that rule, covers every module this increment adds, and passes.

tools/argus-ui/README.md says what the interface now shows, and tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Split from the single UI increment the last cut carried, because the collector and recorder increments together showed how much this half now has to land at once: a second view in a page built for one, a run picker, a second kind of SSE frame, and the whole of a backlog's shape on screen. This increment takes the load-bearing half — the view, its data path and its live update — and the step returns follow in ui-steps.

increments.title: The run view shows every step recorded, collapsed and expandable
increments.goal: Show, inside the run view, every step the backlog holds: the steps recorded against each increment and the run's own steps, each collapsed to a summary line and expandable to the full return.
criteria: Per increment the view shows the steps recorded so far, each with its label, its time and its return, collapsed to a summary line and expandable to the full return.
The run's own steps — the opening cut, each close, the publish — are shown the same way.
An increment with no steps renders as the normal state it is rather than an empty panel that looks broken, which is what a closed increment looks like once the recorder has shed its step returns.
Switching to another run, and a live write to the shown run, both leave the steps on the page matching the state now shown and no step of the state before it.
argus-ui still imports nothing outside itself and reads no uroboros file; test/independence.test.mjs covers every module this increment adds and passes.
tools/argus-ui/README.md, tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md are current for what this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: New, split off from ui: the step returns are the one part of the run view that is its own piece of work — a return of arbitrary shape has to collapse to a line and open to the whole — and it lands on a view that already renders and updates itself.

return.summary: Landed the recorder increment's branch into claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr (fast-forward e3a0cc2..b58a6b5, no conflict) and pushed it, closed `recorder` as done on the review's no-findings verdict, and re-cut the one increment still open. The change against the last cut: the single `ui` increment became two, `ui` and the new `ui-steps`. Two increments' worth of evidence made that split the right one. The collector increment fixed the wire contract (POST /api/runs, GET /api/runs latest-write-first, GET /api/runs/:id, an uncoalesced SSE frame naming only the run and its update time), and the recorder increment proved the producing half is done and untouchable, so everything left is one project's front end: a second view inside a page built for a single one, a run picker, a second kind of stream frame, and the whole shape of a backlog on screen, against an app.js of 751 lines, a page suite of 1015 and a stylesheet of 1072. That is more than one review can judge well. `ui` now takes the load-bearing half — the view exists beside the session view, shows the run's header, its increments with id, title, status, branch and note, the open/closed counts and the codemap, opens on the most recently written run, switches runs, and updates live — and `ui-steps` takes the part that is its own problem: a step return of arbitrary shape collapsing to a summary line and opening to the whole, for both an increment's steps and the run's own, plus the empty-steps state a closed increment leaves behind. Rejected: keeping `ui` whole (one review over ~2000 new lines of view, markup, styles and suites), and splitting instead into a static view and a later live one (the live path is small, and deferring it would leave the risky stream wiring for last). Issue criteria for the front end land as: the header/increments/counts/codemap clause of the big display criterion, the open-on-latest-and-switch criterion, the live-SSE criterion, the independence criterion and the closed-reads-as-closed clause in `ui`; the steps clause of the display criterion, the run's-own-steps clause and the increment-with-no-steps clause in `ui-steps`; documentation currency and a green ./test.sh sit in both, each scoped to what that increment adds. Codemap changes from this increment: the three recorder files move to the already-changed section, since the increment touched exactly them and nothing more; tools/argus-ui/public/format.js is added, hedged, because the view has times to render and format.js is where the page's formatters live; tools/argus-ui/src/config.mjs joins src/server.mjs in the deliberately-excluded list; and the exclusion of the agent pages and workflow prompts is now a fact rather than an expectation, the recorder increment having changed none of them.
